candidate: OpenC Core Candidate 2 — Implementation Readiness Revision 1

terms.definition: one UTF-8 OpenC source sequence assigned to one logical module by declared project context.
the order-independent declaration set formed by all source units assigned the same module identity.
initialized storage with a complete type and active lifetime.
memory capable of containing an object; storage alone is not a value.
the abstract typed result represented by an expression or object.
a copyable non-resource value whose type carries no unique ownership obligation.
the binding responsible for exactly one resource or owning-pointer obligation.
temporary non-owning access through `ref` or a slice.
a low-level address value of type `ptr T` with abstract provenance and offset.
code outside an unsafe region or unsafe function body.
an operation whose validity depends on explicit caller-provided low-level preconditions.
a visible nonzero `status.code` result handled by ordinary control flow.
a defined structured non-recoverable failure that runs required cleanup.
one bounded target-declared consequence of violating an unsafe precondition.
a non-copyable value with one exactly-once outer ownership obligation and zero or more visible nested ownership slots.
compiler-only local evidence connecting one fallible call result to the conditional initialization of exactly its `out` targets.
normal scope completion, `return`, `break`, `continue`, recoverable return, or language-generated checked failure.
the finite side-effect-free expression subset used for module constants, switch cases, and plain field defaults.
the smaller context-only expression subset used by `when`.
a source name associated with one declared value, reference, pointer, owner, output slot, function, type, module, or constant according to its declaration kind.
a type whose size, alignment, value rules, and required fields or members are known in the current translation context.
an expression whose evaluation is completed before the next enclosing sequencing boundary defined by the grammar.
a value result, mutation, ownership transition, cleanup action, diagnostic, checked failure, target fault, or externally visible target action whose order or presence is defined by Core.

an operation whose valid-input contract admits neither recoverable failure, checked failure, nor target fault; internal unsafe work is permitted only when a safe wrapper proves all preconditions for every valid input.
abstract identity connecting a raw pointer to one active object, array, typed-storage lifetime, allocation, or declared target region.
one specific activation of an object lifetime in storage; reconstruction creates a new generation and does not revive pointers or borrows from an earlier generation.
a declared finite capacity of an implementation whose exhaustion produces a structured diagnostic rather than altered language meaning.
a half-open region identified by 1-based logical line and Unicode-scalar column coordinates plus 0-based UTF-8 byte offset and byte length.
a named owner binding, return slot, ownership-bearing aggregate field at commit, or proven owning output slot that can carry exactly one ownership obligation without an unnamed temporary.
a stable live object, eligible field, or element location for which Core defines an address-of result type and lifetime bound.
a word spelling that the lexical phase classifies for fixed language syntax and that cannot be introduced as an ordinary identifier.
a primitive type spelling recognized by type grammar; it cannot be rebound, but may occur as an imported module segment under the explicit module-name rules.
